gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS P1800 takes at most 650 W of solar through its single XT60 input, so the panel in its 600 W kit already uses about 92% of that limit. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 takes up to 1,000 W (12–60 V, 20 A), so its 200 W kit leaves room for about 800 W more panel, but every Elite 100 V2 kit is a pre-order shipping mid-December.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited in both chats), Trek4Tech (cited), SolutionEnergy (cited); theoutageplan.com (cited) would not load (SSL certificate error). StormWatts already gives the Elite 100 V2's solar input as 1,000 W, 12–60 V, 20 A, plus Anker C1000 Gen 2 at 600 W/60 V max and DELTA 3 Plus at two 11–60 V, 500 W inputs. Trek4Tech gives the Jackery 1000 v2 400 W and AC180 500 W solar caps. SolutionEnergy says the C1000 Gen 2 and Jackery 1000 v2 are not expandable and the DELTA 3 Plus is. None of them covers the ALLPOWERS P1800 or its 650 W XT60 limit against its own 600 W kit panel. None says the Elite 100 V2 box has no solar cable, or that it takes B300K only in a bundle with Charger 2 and a DC Hub. Only the P1800 part is new; the Elite figures are already out there.
decides: This supports a split pick. The Elite 100 V2 kits are the ones that can grow most on solar (1,000 W input), but they are pre-orders shipping mid-December. The P1800 + 600 W kit ships now (our table, 2026-11-18). Its panel is close to the station's 650 W solar limit, so a shopper should treat it as full on solar: it refills fastest out of the box (1,024 Wh / 600 W ≈ 1.7 h at rated output) but has almost no room to add panels. For a shopper who wants to add panels later, the Elite 100 V2 + 200 W kit is the one to wait for: 200 W of a 1,000 W input, ≈5.1 h refill at rated output.
